rows.why: Rule 1: all three prongs at 19013 start sub-MIP there and rise away (p4 shows the 19032-19013-19031 chain rising monotonically 10k->205k into a proton stopping at 19012, and 19023 rising to 310k at 19014); competing apex 19003 (two long tracks, 21 cm upstream) has the connecting 23.5 cm segment arriving hot, not leaving cool.

Clean V apex at the lowest z of the event: 61 cm pi rises away to a Bragg end at 16005, 116 cm mu leaves the other way, cluster-68 prong points back at it, and the muon far end 16003 carries the Michel-like stubs (rule 3).
Rule 1 unanimous: 3 of 3 prongs rise away (182 cm mu to 116k, 28.6 cm p to 189k, 56 cm p to 208k, all stopping elsewhere), a 1.4 cm fragment sits 5 cm away, and it is at low z (32).
Deg-4 hadronic knot: 12 cm proton rising away to 213k at 16001 plus two very hot short stubs (187k, 160k), with the MIP muon leaving and continuing through 16000 into cluster 49 to stop 185 cm away.

Leaning on the charge discontinuity at 10002 (256 cm muon flat MIP then a separate 7 cm prong rising 15k->217k plus an 11 cm wiggly prong), but the competing read - a cosmic muon stopping with a Bragg and a Michel at this same end (rule 3) - survives, the 7 cm prong being nearly collinear with the incoming muon.
Deg-3 vertex with a 28.5 cm proton rising away to 175k, a 2 cm 132k stub, and a 139 cm muon leaving downstream; a 2.5 cm fragment sits 5 cm away.

Zoom shows 20004 as the common endpoint of the dark-red 10 cm proton (stopping at 20001, 184k) and of the MIP track that runs up in z through 20008/20010 into the 154+178 cm muon; 20008 3.6 cm away is the only real alternative.

Event is a handful of disconnected dots (rule 8); 19001 is the only multi-prong point, a deg-2 end of the 4.7 cm 226k stopping proton, and the most upstream of that pair, but this is close to a guess.
Rule 1 unanimous 2 of 2: a 97 cm muon rising away to 117k and a 61 cm proton rising away to 220k, both stopping, and the 175 cm EM shower (cluster 126, pi0) starts 12 cm downstream of it.

Trap-2 read of p4: the 5 cm means at 18002 are inflated by an unresolved vertex blob (plus a 1.5 cm 151k proton stub), while both long prongs show their own multi-cm rises at their FAR ends (180k at 18000, 125k at 18001), i.e. both stop away from 18002.

p4 shows the 5 cm prong falling 260k at 17000 to 40k at 17002, so it is a proton starting at 17002 and stopping at 17000, with a 5.9 cm prong and a flat-MIP 129 cm muon also attached; no Bragg anywhere on the muon rules out the stopping-muon-plus-Michel reading.
Deg-3 vertex with two very hot short protons (181k, 196k), a 2.3 cm 175k fragment 1 cm away, and a 198 cm muon rising away to 122k where it stops at 5000.
Only real cluster in the event; p4 shows the 4.7 cm proton rising 110k->240k away from 20002 toward 20001, and 20002 is the deg-3 hub carrying two further stubs.

Zoom shows 7010 as the apex at the lowest z where everything converges: 71 cm mu rising away, 45 cm pi rising away to 150k, the 475 cm muon through 7007, and all the shower clusters (79/72/75/76) opening downstream of it; the 7.4 cm proton reading hot at the vertex is blob contamination.

Rule 8 territory: disconnected low-dQ/dx fragments near the x/y edge with no long track and no real cone (p5 RMS ~1-2 cm); I lean on rule 7 and take the deg-3 hub of the most upstream fragment group (cluster 15, z~232) as the start of the EM activity.
Rule 1: the 162 cm muon rises monotonically onto the stopping-muon template at 14001 and the 16 cm 2-3x MIP hadron is hottest at 14000, so both prongs get cooler toward 14002.

Rule 1 + geometry: 8032 and 8007 are collinear fitter fragments of the 148 cm muon that Bragg-stops at 8001, so the only real kink is 8004, where an 8 cm proton branches off perpendicular and stops at 8000 (257k, proton template).
Rule 1: the event is one ~38 cm object that is MIP (36k) at 9010 and rises to a 210k Bragg at 9004, so 9010 is the cool end it comes out of (and the lowest z).
Three-prong junction: two heavily ionising protons (150-200k) end at 6001 and 6004 and a 33 cm MIP muon leaves toward 6000, all radiating from 6003.

The 135 cm muon leaves 9001 forward in +z and exits at the x=-200 anode (no Bragg there, and its hot end is at the top, so it cannot be a downward cosmic); the segment out of 9001 rises away (51k->66k) and a hot 3 cm 153k proton stub sits 2 cm off 9001.

Deg-3 hadronic hub: the 6.1 cm proton rises monotonically to 262k at 13001 on the proton template and a 3.3 cm 101k stub leaves to 13016; the 143 cm muon starts 1 cm away at 13002, so this is a 1 cm coin-flip between 13015 and 13002.

16004 is the apex of the star at the lowest z in the event (z=16) with every prong radiating in +z; the 38.6 cm muon rises away and stops at 16009, and the 28.2 cm prong stops at 16013 (129k). 16006 is 4 cm along one prong.
Rule 1 on a deg-5 hadronic star: every one of the five prongs is coolest at 23002 and hottest at its far end (209k at 23000, 200k at 23005, 197k at 23001).
Only junction in the event: a 3.9 cm 145k proton stub out to 12002 and a 25 cm MIP muon leaving forward in +z that exits at z=498; 12001 is also the lowest-z candidate.
Rule 7: 11001 (z=88) is the upstream tip of the shower stem; every other cluster in the event is downstream of it and the transverse spread grows with z, so the apex is here.

Everything in the event lies on one straight line in the principal frame; 9000 is the only deg-3 vertex and the only one whose attached segment rises away (43k -> 230k at 9001), but rule 2 would prefer the cluster-50 end 25 cm lower in z, so I am close to guessing.
Rule 8-like: the only real object is one 3.6 cm 194k proton in a field of sub-cm dust, and both its ends read identical dQ/dx, so only rule 2 (3001 is 2.8 cm lower in z) separates the two ends.

Rule 3: the 15006/15000 end carries a 107k Bragg plus a 1.9 cm Michel-like stub so it is the stopping end of the 223 cm muon; 15001 is the other end, starts in the detector interior, and has three sub-cm dust clusters within 6-9 cm.

The 193 cm muon rises monotonically onto the black stopping-muon template at 13001 (230k) so it comes out of 13002, where a 7.3 cm 2x MIP hadron branches off the other way; 13002 is the only junction.

Event is broken into five fragments strung along a 142 cm line near the x wall; 11001 is the cool start (56k) of the only clean Bragg object (119k at 11000, travelling forward in +z) and is the lower-z of the two rule-1 vertices, but I cannot attach the upper fragment chain to it.

Rule 1/6: deg-3 junction at the lowest z (7.3 cm) with two proton stubs whose Bragg peaks (210k, 180k) sit at the far ends and nothing rising toward it, and the three downstream shower fragments (clus 9, 67, 85) all back-extrapolate to it.
Rule 1: deg-2 junction where a 30 cm muon runs off and Braggs at 12000 (116k) and a 6 cm proton runs the other way and Braggs at 12001 (199k); nothing rises toward 12002.

Rules 1+7: p5 cone from 12009 rises monotonically 2.5->26 cm (best apex of the EM complex) and the 69 cm proton (segs 12013+12030, kink at 12004) Braggs at 12013 while its 12009 end starts at 25k -- so 12004's clean '2 of 2 rise away' is a mid-track kink and the x2.09 'rise toward 12009' is a delta blob 6 cm out, not a Bragg.

Rule 1: only real cluster is one 244 cm muon; it is hotter (116k) at 12000 near the bottom wall where it stops and cooler (71k) at 12001, which sits in the detector interior, so the track comes out of 12001; low-z end too.

Rule 1/6 by default: the only junction (deg 3) with vertex-like activity -- pi+, mu and e stubs plus a 4 cm fragment within 5 cm -- at the launch point of the 319 cm MIP muon; caveat, it sits at z=4 on the upstream face so an entering rock muon cannot be excluded.
Rule 1: deg-2 junction with a 4.9 cm proton at 179k (stopping stub) on one side and a 66 cm MIP muon that exits the +x wall (x=201) on the other; lowest-z candidate.
Rule 1/6: the whole event is one 8 cm two-prong -- two heavily-ionising protons (214k, 182k) leaving a single deg-2 junction back to back, with three sub-cm blips within 12 cm of it.

Rule 1: deg-3 junction with an 18.8 cm proton Bragging at 15003 (207k) and a 1.1 cm proton stub, while the 88.6 cm muon leaves and exits the +x wall (x=201); the muon's x1.52 'rise toward' is vertex-region charge in its first 5 cm.
Rule 1 in its cleanest form: 2 of 2 attached segments rise away -- 93 cm muon Braggs at 11000 (121k) and 8.7 cm proton Braggs at 11002 (202k), nothing rises toward 11001.

Rule 1: deg-2 junction with a 25.3 cm proton Bragging monotonically to 207k at 23013, while the other prong is MIP and continues collinearly through 23012 -> clus 9 (9001/9002) and exits at x=201; the other object (clus 17) is a stopping muon with a Michel at 17010 that back-extrapolates to the top face, i.e. a cosmic.

Rules 1+7: lowest-z structure of the event -- a 4.4 cm proton stub at 199k hanging off a deg-2 junction at z=89, from which the whole 100 cm EM shower opens monotonically toward +z; nothing rises toward 8001.

Rule 1: deg-4 junction at the lowest z (155 cm) with an 11.5 cm proton Bragging away to 206k at 11009, a 2.1 cm proton stub at 173k, a 1.5 cm pi+ stub, and the 25 cm electron leaving toward the shower -- 0 of 4 segments rise toward it.

Rule 1 + convergence: the 177 cm muon leaves 19001 and exits the bottom wall (y=-198.6), a 0.6 cm pi+ stub sits on it, and the detached 84 cm EM shower (clus 82) back-extrapolates from its apex 82064 to within 0.2 cm of 19001.
Rule 1: deg-2 junction with a 122 cm muon that Braggs to 104k where it stops at 7000, and a 5.5 cm proton stub at 175-195k on the other side; nothing rises toward 7002.
Rule 1: deg-2 junction, 143.6 cm muon rises x3.05 away to 120k at 14000 and a 5.5 cm proton stub at 152-167k leaves the other side; lowest-z candidate at 427.5.

Rule 1: 16002 is the deg-2 junction where the 241 cm muon starts (it heats x1.34 toward its far end 16000, so it stops there) and a 7 cm ~180k e/cm proton stub hangs off; it is also the lowest-z candidate.

Only structure is one 50 cm flat-MIP track plus a collinear 5 cm stub that runs out of the detector at z~498, so the sole contained end 15001 (lowest z) is the start by elimination; no Bragg or junction evidence, close to a guess.

A single 189 cm muon, flat MIP end to end; 13000 leaves through the bottom wall at y=-198, so the interior lower-z end 13001 is the only possible start, but with no rule-1 or hadronic evidence this is close to a guess.

Vertex knot at x~-178, z~193-195: the 194 cm track starts at 8004 (heats x2.0 toward 8003) and an 11 cm proton with a clean monotone Bragg (145k->300k) stops at 8006; 8004 vs 8005 are 2.9 cm apart and both are rule-1 clean, so I take the lower-z one carrying the long track.

Rule 1 and the two-Bragg trap resolved: from 16004 an 88 cm muon rises to 208k at 16000, a 56 cm muon rises to 205k at 16005, and via the 1.5 cm stub a 22 cm proton rises monotonically to 245k at 16001 - all three stop away from 16004.

The 114 cm muon rises x2.2 to 114k at 15003 where a 7 cm electron segment hangs off (rule 3, Michel at the stopping end), so the far end is 15003 and the vertex is 15004, which also carries a heavy 7.6 cm ~125k pi+/proton stub and is the lower-z end.
Textbook stopping muon: the 158 cm track follows the black template over its last 20 cm up to 165k at 15003, so it starts at 15004, where a 2.4 cm 122k stub and a 2.9 cm 208k proton also sit.

One 360 cm muon that exits the anode at x=-201; its only interior end 17001 (lowest z) has a spray of small low-energy deposits 10-20 cm downstream/below it, and the muon runs +z from there, consistent with a forward beam muon out of this point.
Rule 1: from 9002 the 150 cm muon runs out through z=500 and the 19.5+5.1 cm proton chain rises monotonically along the brown template to 255k at 9001, so both products point away from 9002.

Perfect rule-1 signature - 2 of 2 attached segments rise away: the 58 cm proton reaches 300k at 13000 and the 101 cm muon follows the stopping-muon template up to 140k at 13001; 13002 is also the lowest-z candidate.

Rule 8: the entire event is a 3 cm doubled stub at 16000 plus scattered isolated dots over ~40 cm with no readable direction, no junction of real tracks and no dQ/dx asymmetry, so any click is as good as any other and I abstain.

8001 is the apex of a hot V at the upstream tip of the event: a 13 cm proton rises to 189k and stops at 8010, and the 12 cm trunk rises to 212k into the shower body that opens out downstream (rules 1 and 7), and it is the lowest-z vertex of the cluster.

Cluster 17 is a single 48 cm chain (17003-17036-17002-17000, every vertex deg<=2, straight in the principal frame), cool ~93k at 17003 and rising monotonically along the proton template to 213k at 17000, so rule 1 puts the origin at the cooler free end 17003 - also the lower-z end and the one nearest the small fragment clusters at z=307-331.

Everything hugs the top wall (y~197-200) and the 91 cm muon is flat MIP with no Bragg, so it most likely entered as a cosmic; 19001 is the only degree-2 vertex (muon start plus a 0.8 cm stub) and the lowest-z candidate, but the pick is close to a guess.
Upstream apex of the big shower: from 11002 a 19.6 cm proton rises to 188k and stops at 11009 while the 14.7 cm trunk rises to 191k into the shower that opens out over z=202-280 (rules 1, 2 and 7).
